claim.quote: Experimental Observation of a Heavy Particle J

date.note: Publication date. Ting reports postponing the announcement and telephoning Frascati on 11 November 1974.

key_value.quote: We report the observation of a heavy particle J, with mass m=3.1 GeV and width approximately zero.

name: Experimental Observation of a Heavy Particle J
notes: The paper title says "Observation"; the discovery label comes from the Nobel citation and BNL, so the type follows the title (A16).
The SLAC side of the same discovery is not recorded in this stream.

summary.plain: Ting's group reported a very narrow peak in electron-positron pairs at 3.1 GeV from proton collisions on beryllium at Brookhaven, a new heavy particle they named J. The same particle was found at SLAC at nearly the same time and is now called J/psi.
summary.technical: e⁺e⁻ mass spectrum from p + Be at the AGS measured with a precise pair spectrometer shows a resonance at m = 3.1 GeV with width approximately zero (less than 5 MeV, per Ting's lecture).

title: Experimental Observation of a Heavy Particle J
why_it_matters: The 1976 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Burton Richter and Samuel Ting "for their pioneering work in the discovery of a heavy elementary particle of a new kind"; BNL says Ting's use of the AGS helped confirm the existence of the charmed quark.
